strengths: Clear motivation combining token-level adaptation and test-time scaling insights; well-structured presentation with excellent figures
Thoughtful dual-loss training strategy (Score Dispersion + Distribution Preservation) with careful engineering (buffer control, EMA) to address real challenges in router learning
Practical post-training applicability to existing pre-trained models; demonstrated on both dense (1.7B) and MoE (30B) architectures
Comprehensive evaluation across 17 benchmarks spanning three domains with useful ablation studies and layer-wise token selection visualization
Parameter-efficient approach (<0.1M new parameters) with modest 6.27% FLOPs overhead; consistent improvements without performance degradation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: combines well-established techniques (token selection, dynamic depth) with a training strategy; incremental rather than fundamental contribution
Modest empirical gains (0.87% on 30B model; 1.88% on 1.7B) without statistical significance testing; 6.27% FLOPs overhead for 0.87% gain on large model lacks compelling cost-benefit justification

Missing critical latency analysis: only FLOP analysis provided; actual inference latency during auto-regressive generation not measured; sequential token processing could create significant decoding latency overhead

Insufficient comparison with related work: no empirical comparison with MOR (most similar concurrent work) or ITT; Table 4 describes differences but provides no head-to-head results; missing simpler baselines

Limited experimental scope: post-training only (pre-training unexplored); single model family (Qwen); unclear generalization to other architectures; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Incomplete token selection analysis: visualizations mostly qualitative; consistency of selections across different inputs not established; linguistic properties predicting selection not analyzed systematically

Technical clarity issues: learnable parameter β in fusion strategy (Eq. 4) barely discussed; Pack/Unpack positional embedding reassignment (Eq. 3) lacks theoretical justification; hyperparameter sensitivity analysis incomplete

strengths: Practical post-training applicability: Can be directly integrated into existing pretrained models without retraining from scratch, unlike MOR which requires training from scratch over 200B tokens

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tests across multiple model scales (1B-1.7B dense and 30B MoE), diverse benchmarks spanning general knowledge, mathematics, and coding, with thorough ablation studies

Well-designed training strategies: Dual-loss approach (score dispersion + distribution preservation) cleverly handles gradient vanishing while promoting token selection discriminability; buffer-based threshold control with EMA synchronization is thoughtful
Minimal computational overhead: Achieves ~6% FLOPs increase while maintaining 91.6-93.1% throughput, representing a reasonable efficiency trade-off

Strong analysis and visualization: Demonstrates that selected tokens have higher logit entropy (uncertainty), nested review reduces entropy for selected tokens, and reveals hierarchical layer-wise patterns in token selection
Consistent improvements across diverse architectures: Results hold across Qwen, Llama, and Gemma model families
weaknesses: Significant performance degradation at scale: Shows 1.88%-2.61% improvements on 1B models but only 0.87% on 30B-A3B model, suggesting limited scalability with inadequate discussion of why effectiveness diminishes on larger models—a critical limitation

Limited novelty and incremental contribution: Token selection via routers (MoE), entropy-based losses, and EMA-synchronized threshold control are established techniques; the contribution is primarily their combination

Insufficient baseline comparisons: ITT comparison is cursory; lacks direct empirical comparison with MOR under identical computational budgets; missing comparisons with other recent adaptive computation and post-training efficiency methods

Weak theoretical justification: Fusion strategy (Eq. 4) with β·p_i weighting lacks justification; no ablation comparing alternative fusion strategies; sigmoid routing superiority over alternatives unjustified; entropy-token criticality connection is empirical not theoretical

Limited applicability scope: Only applies to post-training/SFT phase (pre-training impact unknown); only tested on auto-regressive LLMs; requires many hyperparameters with limited sensitivity analysis
Statistical rigor concerns: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; some improvements are marginal (e.g., +0.13 on BBH for 30B model); unclear if gains exceed noise
Reproducibility issues: Code promised 'will be released soon' but unavailable; complex multi-loss training procedure difficult to reproduce; many interdependent hyperparameters
Incomplete hyperparameter analysis: Table 4 ablations limited in scope; impact of batch size, initialization, data composition unexplored; why layers 4:23 optimal not justified

Missing experiments: No direct MOR comparison at 30B scale; no analysis of performance on longer sequences; limited task-specific analysis of why reasoning tasks benefit more (~5% on BBH/GPQA vs. 0.87% average)
